A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StreamingTOM work, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable supplementary Sections A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, token-retention and quantization ablations, and qualitative video-question-answering examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds LongVideoBench evaluation and Qwen2.5-VL generalization results in supplementary Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 reports limited input-format and 3D rotary-position-encoding adjustments for the Qwen2.5-VL application. The core CTR selection and OQM quantization/retrieval mechanisms remain unchanged; Appendix A primarily supplies previously unspecified implementation details.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds LongVideoBench, covering videos lasting 8 seconds to 60 minutes. VideoMME, MLVU, EgoSchema, RVS-Ego and RVS-Movie remain. The Qwen experiment uses the already-covered VideoMME task.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds uncompressed Qwen2.5-VL-7B as an evaluated reference for its compressed counterpart; v1 only cited that model. Existing comparison methods remain unchanged. Table 5 reuses the existing LLaVA-OV-7B reference on the added benchmark.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Qwen2.5-VL-7B evaluation at 32 frames and 0.5 FPS, plus LongVideoBench comparisons between a 32-frame reference and 0.5-FPS StreamingTOM. Existing main-text sampling rules, metrics, memory budgets and decoding settings remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 elaborates the existing RVS protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 newly tests whether the compression framework transfers to another VLM backbone, using both fixed-frame and streaming configurations. The token-retention/quantization ablation in Table 4 and qualitative cases in Figure 4 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Table 4 retains the same disclosure about interpolated 2-bit results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. New Table 5 reports LongVideoBench accuracy of 56.4 for 32-frame LLaVA-OV and 56.3 for 0.5-FPS StreamingTOM. Table 6 reports Qwen VideoMME averages of 61.3 for the 32-frame baseline, 58.9 with compression at 32 frames, and 63.0 with streaming at 0.5 FPS. These are added comparisons, with different sampling conditions explicitly distinguished.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the stated dominant contributor to CTR's O(N+G^2) cost from similarity computation to clustering. The asymptotic bound and compression objective remain unchanged. Simplified partition and quantization equations are equivalent reformulations, and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about training-free causal pre-LLM reduction, complementary quantized memory, accuracy and efficiency. The revised contribution statement foregrounds frame-aligned groups already described in v1 Sections 3.2–3.4.

C2.justification: v2 adds a duration-based explanation for the LongVideoBench findings, architectural applicability conditions, and explicit limitations concerning backbone capability and vision-encoder latency. Section 3.2 expands the temporal-coherence rationale. These qualify and extend the existing interpretation without replacing it.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands reproducibility information: Algorithm 1 specifies two-pass chunked attention and saliency aggregation; retrieval details cover pre-rotary keys, GQA head averaging, per-layer selection, chronological ordering and cache reconstruction. It also documents incremental RVS encoding and question scheduling. v1 provided only higher-level descriptions of these operations; the project link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Research coverage expands substantially, including additional token-merging/pruning methods, dynamic compression, model pruning and tokenized video compression. Section 2 newly acknowledges concurrent hierarchical streaming-token compression work. References increase from 46 to 74; publication and title updates for retained works are distinct from these additions.

P1.justification: The main five-section structure remains. v2 edits the abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion, simplifies mathematical exposition, and adds terminology clarification, acknowledgments and an organized supplement. Most main-text prose and its narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are refreshed and relabeled, including clearer pipeline and encoder labels. Figure 4 and some tables move, and table headings and spacing are revised. The supplement adds Algorithm 1 and Tables 5–6; the existing efficiency plots and timeline retain their content.

improvement.justification: Appendix A improves reproducibility of previously terse saliency and retrieval descriptions, Table 6 provides empirical support for the existing backbone-portability claim, and Appendix D acknowledges concrete latency limitations. These are useful, bounded improvements while the principal results remain unchanged. The new deployment discussion still blurs bounded active memory with the growing historical storage acknowledged in Section 3.4, limiting the strength of its practical conclusions.
